crime_highlights: The appellant came through a rear door of a home, entered a bedroom where the female complainant was asleep
in his dealings with the complainant he threatened to use a weapon
He had cut a phone line in the house
She had earlier tried to get out of the house but had been restrained from doing so by the appellant
the assault had a serious effect on the complainant, who thereafter was fearful for her safety
rationale_highlights: This young appellant, who has also had alcohol problems, has an aboriginal background
persuades me that a somewhat shorter sentence may achieve the sentencing purposes of deterrence and rehabilitation
Substantially based on the particular circumstances of this young aboriginal offender, I would substitute for the sentence of 6 years a sentence of 4 years
note: Court's reasoning on aboriginal background is brief.

crime_highlights: an undercover officer purchased several flaps of cocaine for two hundred and forty dollars after meeting the accused in a local bar
On his person they found a baggie containing 24.7 grams of cocaine and a wallet with six hundred and sixty dollars in cash in it
At the dresser, where the accused was standing, they found scales, twenty-two empty prepared flaps, and cocaine residue
rationale_highlights: I would not accede to the appellant's claims that the trial judge failed to take into account the appellant's aboriginal ancestry
That the trial judge did not expressly mention each of these considerations in his reasons for sentence does not mean he did not consider them
note: Court never says aboriginal status reduced sentence; crime paragraph is long.

crime_highlights: Ms. Poitras pleaded guilty to a charge of theft under $5,000 after stealing a shirt (having a value of $25) from a store in Prince George
She has a record of some 36 offences dating from 1996 to this year, most of which are thefts under $5,000
she re-offended again in 2005, receiving a sentence of 90 days on a PSP
rationale_highlights: The sentencing judge's failure to consider s. 718.2(e) was, in my view, an error
I am also of the view that the offence here did not justify a nine-month sentence, even given Ms. Poitras's record
I find on balance that a sentence of 90 days would have been appropriate
note: Minor theft; aboriginal link is thin in court's own words.
